issue_context.title: wrong behaviour about MySQL certificates for tools
issue_context.body:
expected

```
if the MySQL server has configurated with CA, server and client can communicate on TLS connection.

there are two groups of certitificates: (server CA), (client key and client certificate)

with both group: server/client can verify/authenticate the other side
with only server CA: the client can verify the server from man-in-the-middle attack, but the server can't verify the client. For example, the user created by CREATE USER ... REQUIRE X509 can't login.
with only client key and client certificate: the client can login to the user created by CREATE USER ... REQUIRE X509. But it can't verify the server (may suffer man-in-the-middle attack).
```

ref https://github.com/pingcap/tiflow/issues/6922 https://github.com/pingcap/tiflow/issues/6921

review_comments:
Should we always set this to true?
`Use skip-verify if you want to use a self-signed or invalid certificate (server side)`
https://github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql#tls

There are two things to verify:

- Is the certificate signed by one of the trusted CA's? (like `--ssl-mode=VERIFY_CA`)
- Does the commonName or subjectAlternativeName in the certiicate match the host. (like `--ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY`)

Did we check both with `VerifyPeerCertificate`?
currently we only verify the first one. Wait for PM's decision.

Only validating the certificate is often used when loadbalancers etc. are used and when the certificate that the server provides doesn't contain the hostname of the loadbalancer in the subjectAlternativeName. This is only required when the loadbalancer doesn't do TLS termination.

Having the client validate the cert and hostname is the only really secure option.

I assume that things like `Not After`/`Not Before` and other important TLS/X.509 things are checked by Go in either case.
